title: Singleton Methods and Eigenclasses
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of singleton methods and eigenclasses in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply singleton methods and eigenclasses in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to class-level method lookup and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Singleton Methods and Eigenclasses through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding singleton methods and eigenclasses helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Singleton Methods and Eigenclasses helps you reason about methods defined on individual objects. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Methods defined on individual objects. Then connect it to Singleton classes. The remaining syllabus points—Class-level method lookup—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Singleton Methods and Eigenclasses
content_blocks.code:
class Greeter
  def initialize(name)
    @name = name
  end
  def greet
    "Hello, #{@name}!"
  end
end
puts Greeter.new("Mina").greet
